dialogue_rules: Each narration cue carries one primary idea.
Every explanatory cue causes or interprets a visible change; narration may not merely read labels.
Define a term in plain language before technical qualifications or acronyms.
Show numerator, denominator, workload, boundary, and uncertainty before speaking a retained ratio.

episodes.title: Why Boolean computation matters
episodes.thesis: Boolean computation turns a decision rule into a precise assignment-to-output mapping that can be represented and evaluated in several different ways.
owns: why repeated exact Boolean evaluation is useful
excludes: This lesson motivates exact Boolean computation; it does not establish that CM is the best representation for every task.
teaching_beats: Open with the concrete question: How do we turn a rule that sounds reasonable into something every machine must answer the same way?
Define the lesson's central distinction: A Boolean rule maps every complete assignment of its variables to exactly one true-or-false output.
Construct and orient the stable example `ex-truth-layout-4`.
Toggle one input at a time and trace why the rule's output changes or stays fixed.
Separate the rule's meaning from any later choice of matrix, graph, solver, or packed evaluator.
State the evidence boundary: This lesson motivates exact Boolean computation; it does not establish that CM is the best representation for every task.
Pause for retrieval: Predict the output after one input changes, then explain which part of the rule caused it.
Close by transferring the rule: The stable object is the assignment-to-output mapping, not the syntax or storage chosen later.
visual_spine: A concrete four-input decision rule lights its inputs and one true/false output.
The rule expands into assignment cards that become rows of an output column.
The output column fans into several possible representations, none marked as the winner.

dialogue_anchors.hook: How do we turn a rule that sounds reasonable into something every machine must answer the same way?
dialogue_anchors.definition: A Boolean rule maps every complete assignment of its variables to exactly one true-or-false output.
dialogue_anchors.boundary: This lesson motivates exact Boolean computation; it does not establish that CM is the best representation for every task.
dialogue_anchors.closing: First fix the function; only then choose how to represent or evaluate it.

episodes.retrieval_check: Predict the output after one input changes, then explain which part of the rule caused it.
episodes.closing_takeaway: The stable object is the assignment-to-output mapping, not the syntax or storage chosen later.
misconceptions: Boolean computation is only about one written expression rather than the function over all assignments.
caveats: This lesson motivates exact Boolean computation; it does not establish that CM is the best representation for every task.

episodes.title: Expression, truth table, and Boolean function
episodes.thesis: An expression is syntax, a truth table enumerates evaluations, and the Boolean function is the mapping they denote.
excludes: Matching one or two examples is not equivalence; the declared assignment universe must match exactly.
teaching_beats: Open with the concrete question: If two formulas look different, are they necessarily different computations?
Define the lesson's central distinction: The expression is the written structure; the Boolean function is the output assigned to every input assignment.
Construct and orient the stable example `ex-truth-layout-4`.
Build an expression tree and evaluate it row by row into a truth column.
Rewrite the syntax without changing the truth column, making semantic equivalence visible.
State the evidence boundary: Matching one or two examples is not equivalence; the declared assignment universe must match exactly.
Pause for retrieval: Choose which of two rewritten expressions denotes the same function before the last truth rows are revealed.
Close by transferring the rule: Syntax can change while the function remains identical.
visual_spine: Expression tree and assignment row stay synchronized as gates evaluate.
A second differently shaped tree grows beside the first and produces the same truth column.
Both trees recede while the shared assignment-to-output mapping remains centered.

dialogue_anchors.hook: If two formulas look different, are they necessarily different computations?
dialogue_anchors.definition: The expression is the written structure; the Boolean function is the output assigned to every input assignment.
dialogue_anchors.boundary: Matching one or two examples is not equivalence; the declared assignment universe must match exactly.
dialogue_anchors.closing: Representations may change the structure, but exact semantics must stay fixed.

episodes.retrieval_check: Choose which of two rewritten expressions denotes the same function before the last truth rows are revealed.
episodes.closing_takeaway: Syntax can change while the function remains identical.
misconceptions: A changed expression tree necessarily means a changed Boolean function.
caveats: Matching one or two examples is not equivalence; the declared assignment universe must match exactly.

episodes.thesis: An explicit correspondence matrix is a dense truth-layout obtained by partitioning variables into row and column axes and placing one exact output in each assignment cell.

Construct and orient the stable example `ex-truth-layout-4`.
Partition A,B onto rows and C,D onto columns, then derive binary indices from one assignment.
Fold the truth-table output column into the 4-by-4 grid and query several cells in both directions.
State the evidence boundary: The matrix is a dense output layout; this definition does not make it compact, a solver, or universally fast.
Pause for retrieval: Given one four-bit assignment, choose its row and column cell before the cursors move.
Close by transferring the rule: The matrix changes the layout, not the underlying Boolean function.

One assignment splits into row bits and column bits; two index cursors meet at its cell.

episodes.thesis: Normalization chooses a stable structure, structural keys identify it, and interning reuses the matching node; these stages cooperate but are not synonyms.
